releases.notes:
- Meshnet and Tunnels now each have their own tab, so everything about sharing files is in one place and everything about tunnels in the other.
- When a device turns Meshnet off, it disappears from the others right away (it used to stay for up to half a minute).
- Fixed: the Private Meshnet switch didn't show or work properly.

- Public Meshnet (the new default): everyone on the same Wi-Fi with SynapseVPN and Meshnet on shows up, and you can send each other files without a code. You still accept or decline every file, and the files are encrypted on the way.
- Private Meshnet: one switch (on the Meshnet page or in Profile → Settings). Then only devices you linked with a code can send you files.
- New: Tunnels, under Meshnet. Create a tunnel and you're its host, like a WireGuard server, with your own interface (keys, address, listen port) and a code. Others on the same Wi-Fi join it with the code. It's a private network between the devices in the tunnel.
- Tunnel details like WireGuard's window: public and private key, address, listen port, and every peer's allowed IPs, endpoint, keepalive, latest handshake and live transfer.

- Meshnet works like WireGuard again: devices only connect after you link them with a code, and only devices on the same Wi-Fi (the same router) can see each other. Nothing is linked automatically through your account, and SynapseVPN no longer opens ports on your router.
- Details still shows each linked device's latest handshake and live transfer.

- My devices, anywhere: your phone and PCs signed in to the same SynapseVPN account now link in Meshnet by themselves. No code, nothing to type: SynapseVPN fills in all the WireGuard settings (keys, addresses, endpoints).
- It works over the internet too, for example your phone on mobile data and your PC at home, even when your internet provider shares one address between customers (CGNAT). SynapseVPN punches a direct, encrypted path between your devices, without any server in between.
- Your phone reaches your PCs from anywhere; just keep Meshnet on.
- New Details (on the VPN card and on each Meshnet device), like WireGuard's own screen: public keys, endpoint, allowed IPs, keepalive, latest handshake and live transfer, updated every second.
- The first update check after connecting no longer waits 40 seconds.

- Updates are found reliably: SynapseVPN checks for new versions in a way that also works while the VPN is on.
- If checking for updates fails, the bell says so and has a Check again button.

- SynapseVPN is now on Android: one tap secures your phone with WireGuard over Cloudflare WARP, the same network as on your PC.
- Meshnet works between your phone and your PCs: link with the same 8-character code, see which devices are online, and send files both ways. Received files go to Downloads › SynapseVPN.
- Threat protection blocks dangerous sites, trackers and ads in every app while the VPN is on.
- Link cleaner: share a link to SynapseVPN (or paste it) to remove tracking parts like utm_, fbclid and si=.
- Dark Web Monitor checks your emails every day and tells you about new breaches. Check any password safely.
- Security check-up for your phone: screen lock, security updates, developer options and more. Plus a ping test.
- Sign in with your SynapseVPN account; your choices and statistics follow you between your phone and PCs.
- Updates download inside the app.
